issues.where: the globe itself and the Shake pill, all four screen stills
issues.what: Without words, nothing shows that the globe can be shaken or how. The only cue is the word SHAKE on a button. The globe has no grab, tilt or drag cue, so a stranger learns 'press a button', not 'shake the globe'. If a drag or device shake works, nothing hints at it.
issues.fix: let the idle hint move the globe itself: a small rock of the glass and base with a few flakes stirring, timed with the pill's pulse. On touch, show a brief tilt-phone or drag glyph the first time, so the glyph and the motion carry the meaning, not the word

issues.where: the pulse ring around the Shake pill, tiles 2 to 7
issues.what: The single pulse is very faint. A thin amber ring at low opacity drifts about 8 px out and then turns into a dim halo. On a dark busy picture it is easy to miss, it plays only once, and it lights up the button instead of the globe.
issues.fix: make the ring brighter at its peak (about 2x opacity, warm cream rather than dim amber), pair it with the globe rock above, and repeat it once more after another idle period if nothing has been pressed

issues.where: the glyph at the left of the Shake pill (desktop and tablet)
issues.what: At delivery size the small globe-with-motion-ticks glyph reads as a lightbulb or a head, not a snow globe being shaken. It only reads correctly at the larger phone size or when zoomed.
issues.fix: draw the glyph larger (about 18 to 20 px at 1920) with a clear flat base and a dome, and make the shake ticks short arcs set apart from the dome

issues.where: mark pressed tiles 6, 9, 12, 15 and sound pressed tile 18 (same in set-B-02 and set-B-03)
issues.what: Pressing a mark or the sound control is almost the same as rest: a 1 to 2 px shrink and a slight brightening. Tile 6 looks the same as tile 4. A press gives no clear feedback, especially under a finger on the phone and tablet. The Shake pill, by contrast, gets a clear amber rim when pressed.
issues.fix: give the marks and the sound control the same pressed language as Shake: a soft warm disc behind the icon (about 15% cream) plus the scale-down, so a press reads at once

issues.where: the sound control at bottom right (desktop and tablet) compared with set-A-03
issues.what: On the phone, the sound control sits in a hairline circle that matches the Shake pill. On desktop and tablet it is a bare 12 to 14 px icon alone in the corner. The control family is inconsistent, and the desktop target looks tiny.
issues.fix: use the same hairline circle on every size, or drop it on the phone too. Keep the icon at about 16 px on desktop

issues.where: the three groups of controls along the bottom edge on desktop
issues.what: The marks at far left, Shake in the center and sound at far right are spread across the full 1920 width, like a web page footer. On the phone the controls sit together as one cluster. The desktop spread makes your eye travel and feels less like part of the picture.
issues.fix: on wide screens, gather the marks and sound closer to the Shake pill, for example in a centered row under the base with even gaps, or at least pull them in from the corners

issues.where: the four season marks at bottom left
issues.what: Only brightness and a small glow mark the current season. On desktop the icons are about 14 px, so the active leaf takes a moment to find. The inactive marks on the tablet's warm bokeh (set-B-03, the leaf) have low contrast.
issues.fix: add a second cue for the current season, such as a 3 px dot or short underline beneath it. Raise the inactive marks to about 60% cream, and add a faint dark backing where the backdrop is bright

issues.where: the bottom of the Shake pill and the sound circle on the phone
issues.what: The pill's bottom edge is about 22 px from the screen bottom, inside the 34 px home-indicator safe area, so a thumb going for Shake can trigger the system swipe.
issues.fix: lift the bottom row so it clears env(safe-area-inset-bottom) by at least 12 px

issues.where: the fourth column (held down) in set-B-01, set-B-02 and set-B-03
issues.what: The held-down column is missing from all three sheets, so the held state of every control could not be checked.
issues.fix: supply the held-down tiles so the long-press and held states can be reviewed
